variables.notice_facts:
1. By an agreement dated 12 March 2026 my client agreed to supply goods to you on thirty days' credit.
2. My client delivered the goods on 5 May 2026 and raised invoice 44/2026 for Rs. 4,50,000 on the same day.
3. You acknowledged receipt of the goods in writing on 6 May 2026 and raised no complaint.
4. The invoice fell due on 4 June 2026 and remains wholly unpaid.

issue.issue: Interest rate appears usurious. Courts may reduce it under the Usurious Loans Act 1918.
issue.explanation: Usurious Loans Act 1918 – S.3: Interest rate appears usurious. Courts may reduce it under the Usurious Loans Act 1918.
issue.fix_suggestion: Keep interest rates commercially reasonable (typically below 24% per annum for commercial loans).

cases.before: The Borrower shall pay interest on the outstanding Principal Amount at the rate of 48% per annum ('Interest Rate'), calculated on the basis of a 365-day year and the actual number of days elapsed. Interest shall accrue daily from the date of disbursement and shall be payable in accordance with the repayment schedule set out in this Agreement. In the event of a payment default, default interest shall accrue on the overdue amount at a rate equal to the Default Interest Rate agreed in this Agreement, being 50% per annum, from the due date until the date of actual payment. All interest payments shall be subject to applicable TDS requirements, and the Borrower shall not be entitled to set off any amount against interest payments due under this Agreement.
cases.after_old_repair: The Borrower shall pay interest on the outstanding Principal Amount at the rate of 24% per annum ('Interest Rate'), calculated on the basis of a 365-day year and the actual number of days elapsed. Interest shall accrue daily from the date of disbursement and shall be payable in accordance with the repayment schedule set out in this Agreement. In the event of a payment default, default interest shall accrue on the overdue amount at a rate equal to the Default Interest Rate agreed in this Agreement, being 24% per annum, from the due date until the date of actual payment. All interest payments shall be subject to applicable TDS requirements, and the Borrower shall not be entitled to set off any amount against interest payments due under this Agreement.
